_purpose: Envelope encode/decode cases for every v0.2 inner type and flag combination (plus invalid encodings that must be rejected), full MEDIA_CHUNK transfers with reassembly and content_hash, all three token_payload forms, and an outer-frame example for every frame_type. Known gap, tracked: spec v0.2.1's REACTION type (0x06) and reply_to flag (bit 2) are not yet covered — cases land with the first envelope-codec implementation (see docs/test-vectors/README.md); every invalid case below stays invalid under v0.2.1.
envelope_layout: offset 1: type (1) — 0x01 TEXT, 0x02 ACK, 0x03 CONTROL, 0x04 HANGUP, 0x05 MEDIA_CHUNK (v0.2 set; v0.2.1 adds 0x06 REACTION, cases pending)
offset 2: flags (1) — bit 0 expiry present (TEXT and MEDIA_CHUNK manifest only), bit 1 MEDIA_CHUNK manifest, bit 3 and up reserved and must be 0 (v0.2.1 assigns bit 2 to reply_to, cases pending)
offset 19: timestamp (8) — sender local time, Unix milliseconds, uint64 big-endian
offset 27: expiry_s (4) — present only if flags bit 0; all later offsets shift by 4

envelopes.name: text-min
envelopes.note: Smallest interesting TEXT; body at offset 27

envelopes.name: text-utf8
envelopes.note: TEXT bodies are raw UTF-8; multi-byte sequences must survive round-trips byte-identically

envelopes.name: text-empty
envelopes.note: Zero-length TEXT body is structurally valid

envelopes.name: text-expiry
envelopes.note: flags bit 0: expiry_s (4 bytes, big-endian) at offset 27; body shifts to offset 31

envelopes.name: control-read-receipt
envelopes.note: Payload = msg_id (16) of the message that was read

envelopes.name: control-token-revoke
envelopes.note: Payload = token_payload absent form (0x00) — revokes the stored peer token (spec §3.2.1)

envelopes.name: control-unknown-type
envelopes.note: Unknown control types are ignored (forward compatibility), never errors (spec §5.5)

envelopes.name: hangup
envelopes.note: HANGUP body is empty: the authenticated end-of-session marker

envelopes.name: media-manifest
envelopes.note: flags bit 1: MEDIA_CHUNK manifest; body = chunk_count(4) ‖ total_len(8) ‖ content_hash(32) ‖ mime_len(1) ‖ mime

envelopes.name: media-manifest-expiry
envelopes.note: flags 0x03: manifest with disappearing instruction — expiry applies to media identically (spec §5.1)

envelopes.name: media-chunk
envelopes.note: flags bit 1 clear: chunk; body = manifest_msg_id(16) ‖ chunk_index(4, 0-based) ‖ chunk_data

envelopes.name: unknown-type
envelopes.reason: type 0x07 does not exist (0x06 is REACTION as of spec v0.2.1)

envelopes.name: reserved-flag-set
envelopes.reason: reserved flag bits (bit 3 and up) must be 0

envelopes.name: manifest-flag-on-text
envelopes.reason: flags bit 1 is only valid on MEDIA_CHUNK

envelopes.name: expiry-flag-on-ack
envelopes.reason: flags bit 0 (expiry) is only valid on TEXT and MEDIA_CHUNK manifest

envelopes.name: expiry-flag-but-truncated
envelopes.reason: flags bit 0 set but the frame ends before expiry_s

envelopes.name: ack-body-wrong-length
envelopes.reason: ACK body must be exactly 16 bytes

envelopes.name: control-empty-body
envelopes.reason: CONTROL body must carry at least control_type

media_transfers.name: single-chunk
media_transfers.note: Smallest transfer: one chunk carries the whole attachment; the receiver verifies SHA-256(content) == content_hash, then ACKs the manifest msg_id. This manifest carries an expiry instruction (flags 0x03).

media_transfers.name: two-chunks-boundary
media_transfers.note: 65537 bytes = 65536 + 1: chunk_count = ceil(total_len/65536) = 2; every chunk except the last is exactly 65536 bytes, the last carries the single remaining byte. Content is a fixed SHA-256 counter stream (see generator).

token_payloads.name: absent-or-revoke
token_payloads.note: One byte 0x00. In M2/M3 it means push off; in CONTROL token-refresh it revokes (spec §5.7).

token_payloads.name: present-fcm
token_payloads.note: FCM registration tokens are opaque ASCII; carried verbatim.

token_payloads.name: knock-relay-plane
token_payloads.note: The relay-plane KNOCK payload carries platform ‖ token_len ‖ token without the presence byte; presence is signaled by a non-empty payload (spec §5.4).

outer_frames.name: register-crid
outer_frames.note: One frame per CRID; payload empty.

outer_frames.name: knock-no-push
outer_frames.note: Empty payload: no push token, online/grace-window delivery only.

outer_frames.name: knock-with-token
outer_frames.note: Payload = platform ‖ token_len ‖ token (the peer's push token, prefix-less form, spec §5.4); used once, then discarded by the relay.

outer_frames.name: teardown
outer_frames.note: Client->relay: tear down my bridge. Relay->client: your bridge is gone. Disconnection is an implicit TEARDOWN.

outer_frames.name: topic-bridged
outer_frames.note: Sent to both ends when a topic's second registrant arrives; the joiner then sends M1.

outer_frames.name: knock-fwd
outer_frames.note: Forwarded knock — the relay strips any token before forwarding; payload always empty.

outer_frames.name: session-bridged
outer_frames.note: Sent to both ends on ACCEPT; the knocker then sends S1.

outer_frames.name: pair-data
outer_frames.note: Opaque pairing-handshake bytes; this sample payload is an arbitrary fixed 80-byte string, real M1–M4 bytes live in pairing-handshake.json.

outer_frames.name: session-data
outer_frames.note: Opaque S1/S2 or transport ciphertext; this sample payload is an arbitrary fixed 44-byte string, real frames live in session-handshake.json.
